independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived at the outset: the offset map records Ps 17 as rule "identity" with 15 WEB verses / 15 MT verses, web_title true and mt_title_verses empty, so the superscription is a prefix inside MT 17:1 and the psalm's 15 refs run 1:1 with MT (15 WEB / 15 MT); the row's title pseudo-ref form is the owner-ruled one. Both Hebrew quotes were re-collated in a batch through collate.py: 4 of 4 results return tier byte against the MT 17:1 window (status GREEN), so תְּפִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד (tokens 1-2 of 12, whitespace-delimited in the maqaf-free staged extract) and the echoed prayer-noun תְפִלָּתִ֑י (token 9) are quotation-grade and do sit in one MT verse. The genre label checks against the device inventory: superscriptions entry 17 carries labels tefillah and le_david, and tefillah membership is 5 psalms. Selah cannot be in play: the inventory holds 71 selah verses book-wide and 0 in Ps 17 (unit: verses). The contestable point I re-derived rather than assumed is 17:5's opening תָּמֹ֣ךְ - it is pointed with dagesh plus qamats (U+05BC U+05B8), the infinitive absolute, not the imperative form pointed with sheva, so WEB's declarative rendering “My steps have held fast to your paths. My feet have not slipped.” (web:Ps.17.5) is pointing-consistent, no imperative intervenes between 17:2 and 17:6, and both the row's testimony framing of 17:3-5 and its claim that the next imperative cluster sits at 17:6 survive. Two observations that are not defects: WEB compresses MT's 3 verse-1 imperatives (שִׁמְעָ֤ה token 3, הַקְשִׁ֥יבָה token 6, הַאֲזִ֥ינָה token 8) into 2 English imperatives, so the English-based cluster claim understates the Hebrew; and the "sworn" characterisation rests on 3 asseverative bal tokens across 2 verses (17:3 tokens 6 and 9, 17:5 token 4) rather than an oath formula - register, not a boundary claim. What does not survive is the warrant the rejected_alternative uses to dismiss the 1-2 | 3-5 rival.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative dismisses the 17:1-2 | 17:3-5 rival on a syntactic dependency the MT does not show, leaving the tier-1 mood shift at the 17:2|17:3 seam unanswered.
challenges.evidence: Byte-true verse heads spliced from verse_map_oshb (Ps 17 is an identity psalm, so oshb:Ps.17.N = web:Ps.17.N): oshb:Ps.17.3 opens בָּ֘חַ֤נְתָּ, oshb:Ps.17.4 opens לִפְעֻלּ֣וֹת, oshb:Ps.17.5 opens תָּמֹ֣ךְ - 0 of these 3 verse-initial tokens carries a waw or a subordinator, and no clause in 17:3-5 is governed by a constituent of 17:1-2, so the sustaining relation is rhetorical, not syntactic. The mood boundary the rival runs on is byte-visible in the same window: 17:1-2 carry the imperatives שִׁמְעָ֤ה / הַקְשִׁ֥יבָה / הַאֲזִ֥ינָה plus the yiqtol petitions יֵצֵ֑א / תֶּחֱזֶ֥ינָה, while 17:3 opens a 2ms qatal declarative series בָּ֘חַ֤נְתָּ / פָּ֘קַ֤דְתָּ / צְרַפְתַּ֥נִי (3 qatal tokens in 1 verse). WEB shows the same turn: “Let my sentence come out of your presence. Let your eyes look on equity.” (web:Ps.17.2) is followed by “You have proved my heart. You have visited me in the night.” (web:Ps.17.3). The 5-verse span may still stand on continuity of address, but the filed reason for rejecting the rival is a grammatical claim the bytes do not support.

reviews.reasoning: Both seams of this span re-derived. The 9|10 seam is not merely defensible, it is forced: oshb:Ps.17.9 opens with the preposition מִפְּנֵ֣י, the min-complement of 17:8's imperative תַּסְתִּירֵֽנִי (token 7 of 7), so no strophe can begin at 17:9 and the rival seam at 8|9 would sever a preposition from its governing imperative. The 5|6 seam holds too, and a stronger corroborator than the row files is available: the device inventory records Ps 17 at yhwh 3 / elohim 0, the 3 yhwh tokens sitting at 17:1 (token 4), 17:13 (token 2) and 17:14 (token 3), while the vocative opening the second petition cycle at 17:6 is אֵ֑ל - pointed tsere plus etnahta, hence the divine name El and not the negative or the preposition (a skeleton sweep of that 2-letter string returns 656 verses book-wide and 1 verse in Ps 17, unit: verses, so the toolkit's short-token homography rule required this pointed byte check). Selah is absent from Ps 17 (0 of the 71 inventory verses), so the device note is true and span-scoped. The span stands; both challenges are to how the evidence is stated, inside the fields the seam argument rests on.

challenges.claim: The signal that a vocative-plus-imperative cluster opens web:Ps.17.6 and mirrors the cluster opening web:Ps.17.1 is positionally false in the Hebrew: 17:6 opens with a fronted pronoun plus qatal and its imperatives fall after the etnahta.
challenges.evidence: Byte-true token order at oshb:Ps.17.6 (identity psalm; = web:Ps.17.6), spliced from verse_map_oshb, tokens whitespace-delimited in the maqaf-free staged extract: token 1 is אֲנִֽי and token 2 קְרָאתִ֣יךָ - a fronted independent pronoun plus qatal; the vocative אֵ֑ל is token 5 and carries the etnahta (U+0591), the verse's main disjunctive, so it closes colon A; the imperatives are הַֽט (token 6) and שְׁמַ֣ע (token 9) of 10, both in colon B. At oshb:Ps.17.1 the imperative שִׁמְעָ֤ה is token 3, immediately after the 2-token superscription. The hearing-imperative is therefore verse-initial at 17:1 and verse-final at 17:6: the lexical echo the claim reaches for is real (שִׁמְעָ֤ה / שְׁמַ֣ע, and הַאֲזִ֥ינָה token 8 / אָזְנְךָ֥ token 7), but the position asserted for it is inverted, and 17:6's actual opener - fronted אֲנִֽי plus qatal - goes unrecorded in the signal field.

challenges.claim: web:Ps.17.9 is called the object clause of the imperative at web:Ps.17.8, but that imperative's object is the suffix already inside 17:8 and 17:9 is a min-complement whose second colon carries no relative particle in the Hebrew.
challenges.evidence: At oshb:Ps.17.8 the object of the imperative is the 1cs suffix inside תַּסְתִּירֵֽנִי (token 7 of 7), already resolved within 17:8. oshb:Ps.17.9 opens with מִפְּנֵ֣י (token 1 of 8), a min-preposition heading an ablative complement, not an object clause; and its second colon אֹיְבַ֥י בְּ֝נֶ֗פֶשׁ יַקִּ֥יפוּ עָלָֽי (tokens 5-8) carries no relative particle - the "who" in “my deadly enemies, who surround me” (web:Ps.17.9) is supplied by the English. Stated correctly the warrant is stronger than the one filed, since a min-complement cannot open a strophe; as filed, the seam rests on an English relative rendering and on a grammatical label the Hebrew does not carry.

reviews.reasoning: Verb-person distribution re-derived across the span from the pointed bytes: 17:10 has סָּגְר֑וּ and דִּבְּר֥וּ (3cp qatal), 17:11 has סְבָב֑וּנוּ (qere; the ketiv סבבוני stands unpointed before it) and יָ֝שִׁ֗יתוּ, 17:12 has יִכְס֣וֹף (3ms yiqtol). Second-person address: 17:10-12 carry 0 second-person forms, and 17:13 reopens it with the vocative יְהוָ֗ה (token 2) and חַרְבֶּֽךָ (token 9), so the row places the resumption correctly. Two things I checked and did not file: the enemies' own 3cp verbs already appear at 17:9 (שַׁדּ֑וּנִי, יַקִּ֥יפוּ), subordinated under 17:8's imperative, so the shift is graded rather than absolute - but since 17:9 opens with a min-complement the span cannot be cut earlier, and the seam is right; and pmarks records ketiv/qere at MT 17:11 and 17:14, neither quoted by this row in either witness, so no disclosure is triggered. Selah absence is true and span-scoped (0 Ps.17 verses of 71). One evidence defect remains, in the exemplar list.

challenges.claim: The signal list cites the English phrase at web:Ps.17.12 as one of the third-person verbs, but the Hebrew clause there is verbless and its copula is supplied by the translation.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.17.12 (identity psalm; = web:Ps.17.12) opens דִּמְיֹנ֗וֹ (token 1: noun plus 3ms suffix) כְּ֭אַרְיֵה (token 2: preposition plus noun) - a verbless clause; the copula in “He is like a lion that is greedy of his prey” (web:Ps.17.12) is supplied by the English. The verse's finite verb is יִכְס֣וֹף (token 3 of 7) and יֹשֵׁ֥ב (token 6) is a participle, so the cited English phrase is not a third-person verb in the witness the claim is about. The class claim itself holds on 3 correctly typed exemplars - סָּגְר֑וּ and דִּבְּר֥וּ at oshb:Ps.17.10, יָ֝שִׁ֗יתוּ at oshb:Ps.17.11 - so the span is unaffected and the repair is to the exemplar, not to the seam.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived. oshb:Ps.17.13 opens with the imperative קוּמָ֤ה (token 1 of 9) followed by the vocative יְהוָ֗ה (token 2) and carries 4 imperatives (קוּמָ֤ה, קַדְּמָ֣ה, הַכְרִיעֵ֑הוּ, פַּלְּטָ֥ה), so here the English cluster maps one-to-one onto Hebrew imperatives, unlike the parallel claim made at 17:6. oshb:Ps.17.15 opens with the fronted אֲנִ֗י (token 1 of 7); a skeleton sweep of that pronoun returns 83 verses book-wide and 3 in Ps 17 (17:4, 17:6, 17:15; unit: verses), so fronting recurs in this psalm rather than marking only the close, and the row does not overclaim it. Positive cohesion evidence the row did not use, which cuts against a rival seam at 14|15: a skeleton sweep of the sin-bet-ayin string returns 34 verses book-wide and 2 in Ps 17, and those 2 are adjacent (17:14, 17:15; unit: verses), both tokens carrying the sin dot - יִשְׂבְּע֥וּ (17:14 token 12) and אֶשְׂבְּעָ֥ה (17:15 token 5) - so the root straddles the line the rival would cut. Ketiv/qere: pmarks records one at MT 17:14, realised at tokens 8-9 (וצפינך / וּֽצְפוּנְךָ֮); the quoted clause “men of the world, whose portion is in this life” (web:Ps.17.14) ends before those tokens, so no reading-dependent material is quoted and no disclosure is owed, and this book's recorded variant zones do not touch Ps 17. Paseq at MT 17:1, 17:3 and 17:14 is seg-layer and single-witness, not load-bearing here. 17:15 is verse 15 of 15 on both witnesses (15 WEB / 15 MT). Confidence medium is conservative given the root link across 14|15, but under-calibration in that direction is not a defect.
